newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 7.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 7.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends ***********************************************
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

NEW YORK - Playboy Enterprises Inc says it expects a 13 percent increase in advertising pages for the first half of calendar 1997, including a 17 percent ad page increase for Playboy's fiscal fourth quarter ending in June.

KRONBERG, Germany - Turks living in Germany have emerged as a key target group for television advertisers, media marketing company IP Deutschland says. Ninety-seven percent of Turkish Germans watch television several times a week, compared with 91 percent of ethnic Germans.

LONDON - Britain's tobacco industry has urged the newly elected Labour Party to talk first before implementing its promise to ban tobacco advertising. All three domestic cigarette makers -- Gallaher, Rothmans and Imperial Tobacco -- are calling on government to take into account existing restrictions under a voluntary code.

WILMINGTON, Delaware - Bristol Myers Squibb Co will boost spending for advertising and promotion by $300 million this year and add 1,500 representatives to its sales force, Chairman Charles Heimbold says. The moves are in response to the expected introduction of rival products for treating cholesterol, diabetes and cancer, Heimbold says.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

LONDON - British Sky Broadcasting Plc says it has placed orders for one million set-top boxes as part of its drive into digital television. BSkyB has joined forces with British Telecommunications Plc, Midland Bank and Matsushita Electric in a new company to deliver digital interactive services to television viewers in the UK.

LONDON - UK media and leisure group Pearson Plc would like to take a stake in business daily The Australian Financial Review, a Pearson spokeswoman says. "We are investigating on a fact-finding basis the possibility of taking a stake. We are not yet at the negotiating stage," she says.

LUDWIGSHAFEN, Germany - The first digital television licences have been issued in Germany, clearing the way for a summer trial run, media officials in the western state of Rhineland-Palatinate say. Digital service DF1, pay television channel Premiere and programming package MultiThematiques received broadcasting permits and cable slots from the state private broadcasting authority for a pilot digital television service.

NEW YORK - Television network ESPN Inc is taking its brand of sports journalism to the print world. ESPN, owned by Walt Disney Co and Hearst Corp, plans to debut ESPN Magazine in the first quarter of 1998, the company says.

CORAL GABLES, Florida - Local television newscasts emphasise crime stories by a wide margin over politics, disasters, health and other types of stories, according to a survey of TV news in eight U.S. cities. The findings tended to confirm the television adage "if it bleeds it leads" and bolstered the claims of critics that U.S. television newscasts have become a newsreel of stretchers, body bags, yellow police tape and anguished victims.
LONDON - Britain's ITV's network director Marcus Plantin intends to stand down as later this year, the commercial television network says.

NEW DELHI - Two Indian government departments will jointly present an expansion plan to strengthen the Internet information superhighway in the country, a statement issued by the Communications Ministry says.

AMMAN - Fans of President Saddam Hussein can now send messages to the reclusive Iraqi president on the Internet via an official homepage set up to celebrate his 60th birthday, computer firm Nahj Computer Services says.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

LOS ANGELES - The U.S. Federal Trade Commission has launched another probe of the pricing policies of the six major record labels, industry sources say. "All six labels got an FTC notice last month saying it was opening a preliminary inquiry into minimum advertising price policies," says one executive with a major label.

VILNIUS - Jim Beam Brands Worldwide, owned by U.S. consumer goods giant American Brands, wants to boost its exports of Jim Beam to Lithuania by 15 to 20 percent this year, newspaper Verslo Zinios reports.
NEW YORK - Eastman Kodak Co. expects 75 to 80 percent of its revenues to come from outside the United States in 10 years, Kodak's Chief Executive Officer George Fisher says.
NEW YORK - Viacom Inc is emphasising Blockbuster's core video-rental business, retreating from a plan to push into retailing, the Wall Street Journal says.

KUALA LUMPUR - Malaysia's passenger car sales, including four-wheel-drive vehicles for private use, totalled 28,290 units in March against 19,541 in March last year, the Malaysian Motor Traders' Association says.
ROME - The United Nations Food and Agricultural Organisation forecasts that banana supply will outstrip demand by 1999, leading to unsustainable world surpluses of the tropical fruit.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

TOKYO - A Japanese lingerie maker unveils a new line of women's underwear made from recycled plastic bottles. It takes three and a half 1.5-litre plastic bottles to make a bra and a pair of pants, says Triumph International Japan Ltd, a subsidiary of Germany's Triumph International AG.

MACAU - Th e gangland crime wave sweeping Macau has prompted a run on bullet-proof vests, say local traders. Most clients are policemen, but others are businessmen worried about their personal safety.

LONDON - The latest American trend to hit Britain is canine confectionery. Three Dog Bakery is open for business and hopes to cash in on the country's renowned love for dogs, just as it has done at seven locations throughout the United States.
AMSTERDAM - Dutch consumers will find buying coffee more expensive as Douwe Egberts, the leading Dutch coffee roaster, raises its prices.

BEIJING - A growing club of educated and wealthy consumers is reviving the ancient and tradition of the tea ceremony seeking aesthetic or personal perfection through ritual preparation of the drink, says the manager of the Minghui Tea Garden on the outskirts of Beijing.
